I rewrote `mergeConfig` in `config.mjs` (named export unchanged).

What changed:
- **Validation**: both arguments must be non-null, non-array plain objects (prototype `Object.prototype` or `null`); otherwise `TypeError`. `overrides` still defaults to `{}`.
- **Own enumerable string keys only** via `Object.keys`, so inherited keys are ignored.
- **No mutation / no retained references**: builds a fresh result object and fresh nested objects; nested values from either argument are copied, never shared. Repeated calls with the same `defaults` are independent.
- **Merge semantics**: top-level keys merged with overrides winning; when both sides are nested plain objects, their own immediate fields are merged (default fields preserved); otherwise the override replaces the value, including `false`, `0`, and `null`.
- **`__proto__` / `constructor` safety**: all writes use `Object.defineProperty` on null-prototype objects, so these keys are ordinary data keys (works for `JSON.parse` input) and cannot trigger prototype setters.
- **Value shape**: values must be primitives (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`) or one-level plain objects of primitives; anything else throws `TypeError`.

Not verified by execution — no shell/test runner is available in this environment; only the file content was reviewed after writing.
